expectations.text: Grounded: cites at least two specific facts taken from the project's own files or data (numbers, file names, quoted lines)
expectations.evidence: Cites several facts from the data, and all of them check out: "found SMB churn 48→104/mo Apr→Sep; Q3 net adds 450 = Q2's 450" (CSV: churn 48..104; Q2 net 633-183=450, Q3 net 733-283=450), "SMB MRR +1.2% Jun→Sep, ent +12%" (190100→192400 = +1.21%; 398000→446000 = +12.06%), "SMB NPS 41→29, reply 6→14 h" (6.1→13.9). It names the file: "every figure recomputed from q3_metrics.csv". It also uses notes.md: "last deck forgotten in a week" and "~8 slides".

expectations.text: Outside judge: names a concrete, runnable verification that does not rely on the model grading its own work (e.g. repeated test runs, an independent parser, held-out data, a backtest, outside readers with a rubric)
expectations.evidence: "judge check.py traces each slide figure to CSV rows, tier 1". The brief adds: "First write a script that pulls every figure out of the slides and recomputes it from the CSV rows. Run it on a draft with one planted wrong number to prove it fails." This is an independent parser checked by a planted error. It also proposes outside readers: "4 of 5 cold readers ... (not measured)".

expectations.text: Hard target: states at least one specific numeric target that goes beyond the stated need
expectations.evidence: "target 4 of 5 cold readers name the SMB call in 2 min (not measured)". The brief repeats it: "Target: 4 of 5 cold readers can state the SMB decision within 2 minutes." This goes beyond simply producing ~8 slides.

expectations.text: Tests an assumption: names a belief embedded in the request or the team's framing and says how the evidence tests it (or already tests it)
expectations.evidence: "doubt \"SMB is fine, more logos\" → SMB MRR +1.2% Jun→Sep, ent +12%". The headline reads: "Sales says SMB is fine because sign-ups hit a record, but SMB cancellations doubled. SMB gained the same 450 net customers in Q3 as in Q2, and its revenue barely grew." Sales' belief is named and tested directly against the CSV.

expectations.text: Floor kept: explicitly guarantees the original ask gets delivered regardless of how far the ambitious version gets
expectations.evidence: "0 ┷ floor: 8 slides, every figure recomputed from q3_metrics.csv", plus a "go 0 (floor only)" option. The brief puts the floor first: "deliver plain slides that pass it before going further."

expectations.text: Deeper, not bigger: does not balloon into 3+ new features or new infrastructure beyond the ask; added scope is mostly method, verification and insight rather than breadth
expectations.evidence: The recommended rung is "2 │ the 2 exec decisions on SMB, each argued both ways ◀". That adds method and insight (argue both sides, label trend vs cause) plus a verification script. The only infrastructure-like item is rung 3 ("monthly segment alert, shadow 1 quarter"), and it is offered, not recommended. The "wider" line lists perspectives (analyst/ops/short), not features.

expectations.text: Access audit: names the specific access, data or decisions it needs from the user (or states plainly that none are needed)
expectations.evidence: "access ✓ python3 pandoc gh · ✗ customer base count → no churn rate" names the specific missing data and what it blocks. "deeper per-account churn + ticket export to test the reply-time link" names further data needed. It also states the user's time cost ("you ~20 min") and flags the format as an inferred decision ("slides.md, inferred"). It is terse but specific.

expectations.text: Stops before doing the work and offers the user a clear choice of how far to go
expectations.evidence: Ends with "── reply: go (rung 2) · go 1 · go 0 (floor only) ───". The transcript shows only reads, a tool check and one CSV analysis script. No slides or files were written.

expectations.text: Data insight: computes from q3_metrics.csv that SMB churn and/or first-response time are worsening and uses it to challenge 'SMB is fine'
expectations.evidence: Transcript shows a python3 script run over data/q3_metrics.csv. The response says: "SMB churn 48→104/mo Apr→Sep", "reply 6→14 h", and "Sales says SMB is fine because sign-ups hit a record, but SMB cancellations doubled. SMB gained the same 450 net customers in Q3 as in Q2." It uses these figures to challenge the 'SMB is fine' framing directly.

needs_review: Tool availability "✓ python3 pandoc gh" can't be checked against the fixture. The transcript shows the check command ran but not its output.
Time and cost estimates ("floor ~20 min · rung 2 ~50 min, ~3× tokens · you ~20 min") are unsupported projections. They are labeled as estimates, not facts.
The output format "slides.md" is assumed and labeled "inferred". Nothing in the fixture specifies it.

notes: I recomputed every cited figure from data/q3_metrics.csv with python3, and all are correct. SMB churn: 48→104 (2.17x, so \"doubled\" is fair). SMB net adds: Q2 633-183=450, Q3 733-283=450. SMB MRR Jun→Sep: +1.21%. Enterprise MRR Jun→Sep: +12.06%. SMB NPS: 41→29. SMB first response: 6.1→13.9 h. September's 262 SMB sign-ups is the maximum in the 6-month window, so \"record\" holds within the data and matches Sales' \"more logos than ever\". The response is careful about causation: it calls the churn/response-time link \"a trend, not a cause\" and says there is no active-customer count, so no churn rate can be computed. The weak spot is readability: the terse box notation (\"tier 1; readers t3\") is cryptic. The reader target is explicitly marked \"not measured\", which is honest, but it means the hard target won't be checked at the recommended rung. All 9 expectations pass.
